Monitor

Monitor is the task manager. It shows what monitord reports, for this node or for any node on the mesh: the processes, and graphs of CPU, memory, each disk and each network interface over the last minute. It reads nothing from the system itself, so a node with no desktop can be watched from one that has one. The reasons are in the monitord and Monitor decision.

The window

  • Processes: every process, sorted by any column (click a header; click it again to reverse), filtered by name or command line, or shown as a tree with parents above their children. CPU is a share of the whole machine: one busy core of eight is 12.5.
  • Performance: CPU, memory, each disk and each network interface down the side, each with a small graph. The chosen one fills the rest: a minute's graph and its figures. CPU adds a graph for every logical processor; a disk adds its read and write rates and its filesystems; an interface its receive and send rates.
  • Node: the chooser in the tool bar lists this node and the mesh peers. Choosing one reads that node's monitord as monitord.<node>.bus. The graphs start full: Monitor asks monitord for the last minute first.

Monitor reads once a second. Pause (Ctrl+P) holds the readings still; Refresh (Ctrl+R) reads once.

End task and Kill

End task (Delete) asks the selected process to finish (SIGTERM). Kill (Shift+Delete) stops it at once (SIGKILL). Both act only on this node's processes, as the person running Monitor, and the kernel decides whether they may: the same as kill in a terminal. They are off while another node is shown. Acting on another node, or as another user, is hostd's job.

Agents

Everything in the window is a command or a verb, under monitor:

VerbBodyDoes
monitor.info—The window's state: node, page, section, sort, filter, selection, and the latest readings
monitor.rows—The process rows in the order shown
monitor.nodenode (a name, or null for this node)Watch another node
monitor.tabtab (processes or performance)Show a page
monitor.sectionsection (cpu, memory, disk:<name>, net:<name>)Show one performance section
monitor.sortcolumn, optional reverseSort the table
monitor.filtertextFilter the table
monitor.treeonTree or flat
monitor.selectpid (or null)Select a row
monitor.refresh—Read the node now
monitor.commands, monitor.executeidList and run commands (process.end, view.pause, ...)
monitor.dialog, monitor.theme, monitor.show, monitor.quit, monitor.pingAs every MixOS app

The window's drive verbs (monitor.ui.*, monitor.window*) are the toolkit's, described in driving an app.

send monitor monitor.node node=beta
send monitor monitor.sort column=memory
send monitor monitor.rows

Running it

monitor [--node NAME] [--noded-url URL] [--service NAME]

A second launch raises the first window. --node starts on a mesh node instead of this one.

Testing

cargo test -p monitor -p vitals

The engine (vitals) is tested without a window or a Bus. The window is checked by offscreen snapshots (apps/monitor/tests/snapshots/); run with UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 to redraw them, and look at the images before committing. The snapshot suite also times the representative workload, a 2,000-process table and a 64-core grid, and prints it.

Macro Bus verbs

The shared macro Bus surface uses this process's catalogue and runner. Subscribe to <service>.macros.finished for completion, where service is the instance’s registered Bus name (for example term-1234 for a second Term instance). Verbs keep the app’s canonical prefix, such as monitor.macros.run.

VerbArgumentsResult
monitor.macros.list{}Catalogue and diagnostics
monitor.macros.reload{}Catalogue and diagnostics
monitor.macros.run{id}Acceptance and run number
monitor.macros.status{}Current or last run
monitor.macros.output{}Retained output and dropped flag
monitor.macros.stop{}Whether termination was requested
monitor.macros.new{title}Create a user per-app macro; {id,title,path}, without opening an editor
